I have a complete picture. Here is my thorough report.

## 1. Build system, Spring Boot version, package structure

- Build system: Maven. Root POM at `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml` (Maven wrapper `mvnw` present; no Gradle).
- Coordinates: `org.springframework.samples:spring-petclinic-rest:4.0.2` (`pom.xml:6-8`).
- Spring Boot version: `4.1.0` via parent (`pom.xml:13-16`). Java version property and OfficeFloor version: `<officefloor.version>4.0.2</officefloor.version>` (`pom.xml:31`). Uses `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (`pom.xml:91`).
- Base package: `org.springframework.samples.petclinic`. Relevant sub-packages:
  - `...rest.escalation` — OfficeFloor escalation (exception) handlers.
  - `...rest.function.owner` — business functions + their exception classes.
  - `...rest.dto` — OpenAPI-generated DTOs (`ProblemDetailDto`, `ValidationMessageDto`), generated from `openapi.yml` by the openapi-generator plugin (`pom.xml:372-382`, `<library>spring-boot</library>`).

## 2. How escalation (exception) handling works

There is NO `@RestControllerAdvice`/`@ControllerAdvice`. OfficeFloor maps a thrown exception to a handler class via one YAML file per exception type under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/`. Each YAML has the form:
```yaml
handle:
  class: <fully-qualified handler class>
```

The 14 escalation YAML files and their target handlers:

| YAML file | Handler class |
|---|---|
| `java.lang.Exception.yml` | `GeneralExceptionHandler` |
| `org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException.yml` | `DataIntegrityViolationExceptionHandler` |
| `org.springframework.web.bind.MethodArgumentNotValidException.yml` | `ValidationExceptionHandler` |
| `org.springframework.security.authorization.AuthorizationDeniedException.yml` | `ForbiddenExceptionHandler` |
| `...rest.escalation.NotFoundException.yml` | `NotFoundExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.CityAtCapacityException.yml` | `CityAtCapacityExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.DailyLimitExceededException.yml` | `DailyLimitExceededExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.DisposableEmailDomainException.yml` | `DisposableEmailDomainExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.DuplicateIdentityException.yml` | `DuplicateIdentityExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.FutureRegistrationDateException.yml` | `FutureRegistrationDateExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.InvalidEmailException.yml` | `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.InvalidPostcodeException.yml` | `InvalidPostcodeExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.InvalidTelephoneException.yml` | `InvalidTelephoneExceptionHandler` |
| `...function.owner.MissingOwnerFieldsException.yml` | `MissingOwnerFieldsExceptionHandler` |

## 3. Where 400 / 409 / 429 originate and how they are currently rendered

All handler classes live in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/escalation/`.

### Status 400 (BAD_REQUEST)

## Summary

I converted every rejection handler that was still emitting a plain `Map.of("errors", …)` body over to RFC7807 `application/problem+json`, using the existing `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper already used by the validation/500/403 handlers. That helper populates all four required members — `type` (`about:blank`), `title` (exception simple name), `status` (via `ProblemDetail.forStatus`), and `detail` — and OfficeFloor serializes `ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>` as `application/problem+json`.

Handlers updated (HTTP status codes unchanged):

- **400** — `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler`, `InvalidTelephoneExceptionHandler`, `InvalidPostcodeExceptionHandler`, `DisposableEmailDomainExceptionHandler`, `FutureRegistrationDateExceptionHandler`, `MissingOwnerFieldsExceptionHandler` (its field list is preserved as a `fields` problem property)
- **409** — `DuplicateIdentityExceptionHandler`, `CityAtCapacityExceptionHandler`
- **429** — `DailyLimitExceededExceptionHandler`

The `MethodArgumentNotValidException` path was already problem+json, so I left it as is.

Test result: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.
